---
title: "Variable and value labels"
---

Parquet holds values, not labels. ggpclient keeps the labels of every `.dta`, `.sav` and `.rds` file, as haven reads
them, in a `meta.json` next to its parquet file. Variable names are lower case, in the parquet files and in their
`meta.json` (`DEM01` in a download is `dem01`); the raw downloads keep the portal's names.

## Labelled data in R

`ggp_read()` reads `.dta`, `.sav` and `.rds` with haven and keeps the labels:

```r
x <- ggp_read("data/download/raw/ggs-ii/w1/at/ggs2_w1_at_v1.1.dta")
attr(x$dem01, "label")             # "Gender"
haven::as_factor(x$dem01)          # the value labels as factor levels
ggp_read("....dta", labelled = FALSE)   # the codes only, as in the parquet files
```

## From the parquet files

`ggp_label()` puts the labels of a parquet file's `meta.json` back on its data, as haven labelled columns:

```r
path <- "data/download/consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.parquet"
df <- ggp_read(path, col_select = c("ggp_country", "dem01"))
df <- ggp_label(df, ggp_meta(path))   # ggp_meta() reads the meta.json next to the parquet

attr(df$dem01, "label")               # "Gender"
haven::as_factor(df$dem01)            # the labels instead of the codes
haven::as_factor(df)                  # every labelled column at once
```

Codes without a label keep their value. `columns = "dem01"` labels only those columns.

The labels themselves:

```r
meta <- ggp_meta(path)
meta$column_labels$dem01      # "Gender"                                  variable -> variable label
meta$value_labels$dem01       # list(`1` = "Male", `2` = "Female", ...)   variable -> value -> label
```

JSON keys are text, so codes are `"1"`, not `1`. Letter codes such as `"b"` are Stata's extended missing values (`.b`).
`ggp_meta(path)` returns the same list for one `.dta`, `.sav` or `.rds` file.

## Per-file meta.json

| key | content |
|---|---|
| `file` | the source file, under `download/raw` |
| `file_label` | the file's own label (empty: haven does not expose it) |
| `column_labels` | `{variable: label}` |
| `value_labels` | `{variable: {value: label}}` |
| `missing_ranges` | `.sav` only: the values SPSS treats as missing |
| `original_types` | the Stata or SPSS display format of each variable |

## Consolidated meta.json: harmonized labels

Countries label the same variable and the same values differently: "Czechia" or "Czech Republic", or `region` 1 meaning
"East Austria" in one country and "East Midlands" in another. The consolidated `meta.json` has one harmonized set:

- **One vote per country**, that of its first file (Belarus ships GGS-II wave 1 in English and in Russian; the English
  file votes). Harmonized Histories and Additional Datasets, which have no country, vote per file.
- **Every variable has one label**: the one most countries use.
- **Every value has exactly one label**: the one more than half of the countries use (ISO 203: "Czechia"). With no
  majority, all labels are joined into one, most used first (`region` 1: "East Austria / East Midlands / ..."). Spelling
  and case variants count as the same label.
- **Several values may share a label**: `dem07` 2102 (Austria) and 3103 (Croatia) are both "Elementary school".
- **Codes are never changed**: the data is exactly what each country delivered.
- **`original_labels`** lists, for every value labelled differently in any file, each wording and the files that use it.

The labelled Stata files from `ggp_stata()` use these same labels. Stata attaches value labels to whole numbers only, so
they go on integer columns and on decimal columns that hold only whole numbers.
